Vivek / Karthik — quick notes (copying the short table I attached):

1) Unit & granularity
- Billing unit: 1 token (we count tokens in the same way as our tokenizer; input + output).
- Granularity: integer tokens. We round up to the next whole token (no fractional token billing).

2) Per-call floor (hosted standard)
- Standard per-API-call billing floor: 10 tokens. That means if input+output <= 10 tokens we bill 10 tokens. After the floor, we bill exactly input+output tokens (rounded up to whole token).
- For Dedicated/Reserved customers we can set a lower floor (e.g., 1 token) as part of contract terms.

3) Long prompts & KV/prefix caching
- Billing model: we bill based on logical tokens present in the request to the API (input + output). If you re-send the same large context each call, you will be billed for those input tokens each time.
- Session aggregation: for interactive sessions you can enable our "context-snapshot" feature — when enabled we store a canonical snapshot of the prefix server-side and accepts a lightweight session_id in subsequent calls. In that mode, subsequent requests that reference the snapshot are billed only for the new tokens appended + the output. (The original snapshot upload is billed once.)

4) Streaming & partial tokens
- Streaming does not change token counting — tokens are counted as they are emitted; billing rounds up to whole tokens. There is no separate micro-token prorating for partial bytes sent.

5) Examples (paste-ready):
- Example A — one-off long prompt:
  • Input: 12,500 tokens
  • Output: 300 tokens
  • Billing: 12,500 + 300 = 12,800 tokens billed (rounded to integers; floor not applicable because >10)

- Example B — interactive session without snapshot (every call includes full history) for 3 calls:
  • Call 1: input 2,200 tokens, output 150 tokens => billed 2,350 tokens
  • Call 2: input 2,250 tokens (history + small edit), output 40 tokens => billed 2,290 tokens
  • Call 3: input 2,300 tokens, output 120 tokens => billed 2,420 tokens
  • Total billed = 7,060 tokens

- Example C — interactive session with context-snapshot (recommended for repeated prefixes):
  • Upload snapshot: 9,800 tokens (billed once)
  • Call 1: new input 40 tokens, output 80 tokens => billed 120 tokens
  • Call 2: new input 15 tokens, output 65 tokens => billed 80 tokens
  • Call 3: new input 25 tokens, output 50 tokens => billed 75 tokens
  • Total billed = 9,800 + 275 = 10,075 tokens (significant savings vs re-sending full prompt each call)

6) Discounts & packaging notes
- For deals we commonly offer: reduced per-token price tiers and the ability to change the per-call floor for Dedicated customers. For example, an enterprise SOW can set the floor to 1 token and apply a 10–25% committed-volume discount.

I'll attach the small example sheet (pricing-matrix-May2026.xlsx) — Vivek, feel free to share that with Alicia and her finance contact.

— Marissa

Hi Alicia — thanks for the patience. Below is a concise, paste-ready summary you can include in the SOW + two quick recommendations to reduce billable token volume. I attached a short example workbook (billing-examples-20260521.xlsx) with the math.

Plain-English summary (for the SOW)
- Billing unit: 1 token; total billed = input_tokens + output_tokens (tokenizer-aligned, rounded up to whole tokens).
- Per-call floor (standard hosted): 10 tokens. Dedicated/reserved contracts can set a lower floor (often 1 token) as a negotiated term.
- Long prompts: billed every time they are included in the request. To avoid repeated billing for the same large context, use our context-snapshot/session_id feature — the snapshot upload is billed once; subsequent calls are billed for appended/new tokens + outputs.
- Streaming: tokens counted as emitted; still integer-token billing.

Paste-ready examples (you can copy these into the SOW):
1) One-off long prompt => billed tokens = input + output
   • Input 12,500 + Output 300 => 12,800 tokens billed
2) Multi-turn without snapshot (each call includes full history) => sum of each call's input+output
   • Call 1: 2,200 + 150 = 2,350
   • Call 2: 2,250 + 40 = 2,290
   • Call 3: 2,300 + 120 = 2,420
   • Total billed = 7,060 tokens
3) Upload snapshot once + interactive calls => billed snapshot once, then only new tokens
   • Snapshot upload: 9,800 tokens (billed once)
   • Call 1: 40 + 80 = 120
   • Call 2: 15 + 65 = 80
   • Call 3: 25 + 50 = 75
   • Total billed = 9,800 + 275 = 10,075 tokens

Recommendations to reduce costs
- Use context-snapshots for large, stable prefixes (saves if you have >1 subsequent call referencing the same prefix).
- For latency-sensitive small calls, consider a Dedicated tier with negotiated per-call floor (e.g., 1 token) and committed-volume discounts — we can model the math in the SOW.

Next steps
- I attached the workbook with the calculations. If you want, I can: 1) produce the same examples priced at your expected committed rate, or 2) schedule a 30-min walkthrough with pricing to finalize SOW language. Which do you prefer?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this week.
